answer: When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 3 times its size, so a group of 7 keys loses far more than 7 single identities would. The kernel graph is rebuilt each epoch, and therefore the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the pigment audit merges it again. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the lantern checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 12 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
